newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Chiron Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Chiron Q2 results.

text.p: Chiron Corp Wednesday reported second quarter financial results. The following is a copy of the company's news release.
EMERYVILLE, Calif., July 23, 1997--Chiron Corporation (NASDAQ:CHIR) reported today its second quarter 1997 results.

For the second quarter ending June 30, 1997, operating income rose 72% from $16 million in 1996 to $27 million in 1997 and net income rose 3% from $15 million to $16 million for the same period. Revenues in the second quarter increased from $316 million in 1996 to $334 million in 1997 or 6%.

Chiron's results for the second quarter of 1996 included a $12 million pretax gain arising from the sale of its 50 percent interest in a generic chemotherapeutics business (CBVT) to its partner Ben Venue Laboratories, Inc.

Excluding the sale of CBVT in 1996, net income rose 122% in the second quarter of 1997. Contributing to operating income were strong performances in the Chiron-Behring joint venture, acquired in July 1996, the Chiron-Ortho joint business and increases in collaborative agreement revenues in the second quarter of 1997. Second quarter 1997 earnings per share was unchanged at 9 cents per share versus prior year due to the 1996 second quarter $12 million gain from the sale of CBVT.

For the six months ended June 30, 1997, Chiron reported net income of $31 million or 18 cents per share on revenues of $664 million compared to net income of $28 million or 16 cents per share on revenues of $621 million for the first six months of 1996, an increase in net income of 11 percent.

Net product sales for the second quarter increased from $254 million in 1996 to $256 million in 1997, an increase of $2 million between years. Product sales in the second quarter of 1997 were dampened by unfavorable foreign currency exchange rates which, when compared to rates in effect last year, reduced the increase by $11 million, or 4 percentage points of revenue growth. Compared to the second quarter of 1996, product sales increased in Chiron's Diagnostics and Therapeutics businesses.

During the second quarter of 1997, sales of branched DNA probe kits increased $7 million, or 87% reflecting the continued overall growth in the viral load testing market for HIV. In addition, a 10% increase in assay volume during the second quarter of 1997 drove a $6 million increase in sales of ACS immunodiagnostic products between years.

Ophthalmic product sales decreased 11% in the second quarter of 1997 due to softening in the market for PMMA intraocular lenses and the impact of competing products, reduced sales of Vitrasert(R) and the impact of unfavorable foreign exchange rates as compared to the prior year. Vaccine product sales from Chiron's Italian subsidiary decreased 12% in the second quarter of 1997, primarily due to the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against the Lira and a reduction in sales of pediatric oral polio vaccines due to supply constraints.

Equity in earnings of unconsolidated joint businesses increased $8 million in the second quarter of 1997, after adjusting for $1 million of 1996 earnings from CBVT, which Chiron sold in May 1996. Chiron's share of second quarter earnings from its 49 percent interest in the Chiron-Behring joint venture contributed $6 million to this increase. In addition, 13% revenue growth in the Chiron-Ortho joint business resulted in $3 million of the increase in equity in earnings of unconsolidated joint businesses in the second quarter.
During the second quarter of 1997, a $7 million reduction in cost of sales was realized within Chiron Diagnostics due to a revised estimate of royalties to be paid on sales of certain products.
Collaborative agreement revenues in the second quarter increased from $23 million in 1996 to $29 million in 1997, reflecting license fees and increased research funding from Novartis.

In July 1997, an FDA advisory panel endorsed the efficacy and the safety of Regranex(R) (becaplermin) for the treatment of diabetic ulcers that occur on the lower limbs and feet. Diabetic foot ulcers are a serious complication of diabetes affecting 1.5 million patients each year. Through a collaboration with R.W. Johnson Pharmaceutical Research Institute, Chiron will manufacture and supply Regranex which will then be marketed in the U.S. by Ortho-McNeil Pharmaceutical, a Johnson & Johnson company.

Chiron expects the FDA to complete its review of DepoCyt(TM) (injectable sustained-release cytarabine) by year end 1997. Chiron and Depo Tech Corporation submitted their New Drug Application (NDA) earlier this year for use of this product in patients with neoplastic meningitis.

In further support of its strategy to more aggressively pursue immunotherapy, Chiron submitted a supplemental biological License Application seeking approval to market Proleukin(R) (aldesleukin, recombinant IL-2) for the treatment of metastatic melanoma. Again, a decision is expected from the FDA by year end 1997.

In June 1997, Chiron Diagnostics reached an agreement with Premier, the nation's largest health care alliance, to supply immunochemistry analyzers and supplies to Premier hospitals. As a result of the agreement, Chiron became one of two select suppliers to Premier for certain immunodiagnostic equipment and supplies.
Chiron Corporation is a science-driven, market-directed health care company that combines diagnostic, vaccine and therapeutic strategies for controlling disease.
